chunks: Muḥammad ibn Nuṣayr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
“One afflicted with overpowering bowel disturbance performs wudu (ablution), then returns to his salat (prayer) and completes what remains.”

key_terms.صَاحِبُ: the person characterized by or afflicted with the stated condition
key_terms.ٱلْبَطَنِ: the bowels or stomach, referring here to intestinal disturbance
key_terms.ٱلْغَالِبِ: overpowering or prevailing, indicating loss of normal control

ai.seo_question: What should a person with overpowering bowel disturbance do if it affects him during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one overcome by a bowel-related condition during salat (prayer). He is to perform wudu (ablution) and then return to complete the remainder of his prayer, showing a practical ruling concerning ritual purity and continuity of worship.
